name: Tahini Lentils
assumptions: Yield estimated from typical BBC Good Food / similar lentil-vegetable stir-fry recipes that serve 2 adults as a main dish with these quantities (e.g. 250g lentils + 500g+ vegetables).

Preparation time summed from explicit instruction timings (2 min onion + 5 min vegetables + 2 min final mix) plus ~6 min estimated for chopping, measuring, and mixing tahini dressing; rounded conservatively.
All ingredients screened as listed; no unlisted sauces, stocks, or accompaniments assumed present.
Tahini classified as containing sesame; no tree-nut, soy, or other allergen ingredients appear in the provided list.
Gluten-free confirmed: no barley/rye/wheat/oats listed and all components (lentils, vegetables, tahini, oil) are naturally gluten-free when uncontaminated.
Vegan/vegetarian/dairy-free confirmed by source labels and ingredient list (no animal products).
Pescatarian true because recipe contains no meat but is compatible with fish/seafood consumption.
instructions:
In a jug, mix the tahini with the zest and juice of the lemon and 50ml of cold water to make a runny dressing. Season to taste, then set aside.
Heat the oil in a wok or large frying pan over a medium-high heat. Add the red onion, along with a pinch of salt, and fry for 2 mins until starting to soften and colour. Add the garlic, pepper, green beans and courgette and fry for 5 min, stirring frequently.
Tip in the kale, lentils and the tahini dressing. Keep the pan on the heat for a couple of mins, stirring everything together until the kale is wilted and it’s all coated in the creamy dressing.
